limitations: Outer status-cache, request dispatch/retry and account-generation/refresh ownership model. The host must keep one native bridge identity within each account generation and call refreshNativeAccount when that owner changes.
Two requests and one refresh, or two requests and two overlapping refreshes. Integer identities never wrap. These checks do not establish unbounded population or refresh behavior.

Readiness abstracts ensure() completion. Shared startup coalescing, internal polling cadence, physical timer accuracy and late native startup effects require a separate inner-protocol model. Existing real-client checks exercise normal startup, failure and retry paths.
Only RUNTIME_NOT_READY bridge rejection authorizes the single retry. The bridge must truthfully mean the request was not dispatched. HTTP 503/body codes and ordinary errors never authorize retry.
Conformance runs all 15 named tests through the actual TypeScript client with controlled native boundary ports. It is not generated-trace refinement or installed-device proof.

Native invocation and response publication are fenced. Already-invoked native effects cannot be undone. Native method execution, JSON decoding, request-body admission, HTTP transport cancellation and external account credential storage are outside this instance.
No in-repository production construction was found. The factory is exported for host consumers, whose implementation and deployment coverage remain unknown.
The model groups terminal failures and does not refine exact exception messages or error precedence after refresh. The real-client suite checks observed rejection behavior.
